clinician.trajectory_summary: A 1-year-old male presented with a 2-week history of limp, fever, and difficulty moving the left leg. Initial workup revealed leukocytosis and a radiolucent lesion with periosteal reaction at the left proximal tibial meta-diaphysis on plain radiography. Osteomyelitis was suspected, leading to curettage of the lesion. Histopathological examination of the biopsy confirmed Langerhans cell histiocytosis, showing diffuse mononuclear cell infiltration with positive immunostaining for CD1a, S-100, and CD207, and no BRAF-V600E mutation. Initial staging with skeletal survey, bone scan, and brain MRI showed no other lesions or multisystem involvement. However, two months post-curettage, a new painless mass with an osteolytic lesion was observed in the left fronto-temporal area, leading to a diagnosis of multifocal osseous LCH. The patient was then started on chemotherapy with vincristine and prednisolone.
